findings.title: Tilt labels inverted: campus ≈49° called 'steepest', pucks ≈67° called 'shallowest' — backwards under the elevation convention the docs themselves use
findings.detail: Delta-introduced by the W4 fix. The numbers (~49–67°, campus 49, pucks 67) are correct, but 67° elevation is the MOST top-down/steep end (the deleted code comment called ~66° 'steep'); campus's 49° is the shallowest/most-oblique. The user is live in Blender against these tables — the adjectives mis-orient expectations for the biggest terminals. Repeated in 4 committed copies + the PR body.
findings.recommended_fix: Swap the labels (pucks ≈67° steepest, campus ≈49° shallowest) in spec §0, README, both gen_sprites.py comments, and the PR body.

findings.title: Order pin covers 2 of 3 copies: the committed sprites.json 'order' array — the copy the renderer actually binds bboxes by — is never compared to files[]
findings.detail: sprites_parse_boxes binds bboxes[i] positionally by the json's own order array while textures[i] bind by files[]. A consistent SPRITE_ORDER+files[] reorder without a Blender re-render (CI has none), or a hand-edited/stale sprites.json, passes gate 7 green yet mis-crops at runtime — the B1 class. Verified: committed json order == files[] today; the gate reads only GEN and ODIN. Land the extension BEFORE the fold-in re-render/T2 re-bless.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend test_sprite_order.py: json.load assets/sprites/sprites.json, assert order == files[] (pure text, no Blender).

findings.title: gen_sprites.py docstring documents output in the pre-fix (drifted) order — contradicting SPRITE_ORDER 60 lines below in the same file
findings.detail: Delta-introduced: the fix commit's rewritten docstring says 'Output: …{house_0..3, host, dc, small_biz, campus, puck_1..3}.png' — small_biz/campus before the pucks, exactly the B1 drift this PR fixes — while SPRITE_ORDER pins pucks at 6-8. Verified verbatim at line 25.
findings.recommended_fix: Reorder the docstring list to '{house_0..3, host, dc, puck_1..3, small_biz, campus}.png'.

findings.title: Lint gate 7 ships without a negative-leg self-test — repo convention is that drift gates prove they bite (ci-local 'W1 drift-rejection negative test' row)
findings.detail: The gate's failure path is pinned nowhere in-repo. It bites TODAY (Perkins mutation-tested both legs), but a comparator regression (e.g. accidentally order-insensitive compare) would pass CI unflagged — the exact class the repo's W1 drift-check and a11y-oracle negative legs exist to prevent. Convention verified at ci-local.sh:60.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a self-test leg (drifted fixture asserts rc=1) run from gate 7 alongside the live check.

findings.title: Spec §2 way-2 still promises a sculpted fold-in path that does not exist — still present since round 1, while the PR body claims 'all 6 warnings folded'
findings.detail: Way-2 says 'export the PNGs yourself; the minion folds them in (bbox regen + T2 re-bless)' — but main() unconditionally re-renders all 11 sprites from the SPEC table, overwriting the user's exports. No bbox-only mode. The user is live in Blender NOW; this is the path they will hit. PR body overclaims (W1-W4 only were folded).
findings.recommended_fix: Add a --bbox-only mode (skip render, recompute content_bbox from existing PNGs) or reword way-2 to 'lands with the fold-in commit'.

findings.title: README 'Export names (pinned by sprites.odin)' section lists a different order than the pin it cites — still present since round 1 (was N5)
findings.detail: Under a header claiming the pin, the list shows small_biz/campus before puck_1..3 while files[] pins pucks at 6-8. Third variant of the order story; invites hand-export drift — the user exports PNGs by this list. Upgraded from r1 note: it now sits under an explicit 'pinned by' claim added post-B1.
findings.recommended_fix: List the names in the actual pinned order (puck_1..3 before small_biz, campus).

findings.title: Zero-alpha render emits a negative bbox into sprites.json and exits 0 — no generator-side guard
findings.detail: If a sprite renders empty, content_bbox returns [256,256,-256,-256], the run reports success, and only the renderer-side range check catches it later (whole-sheet failure, primitives fallback). Assert 0<w, 0<h in the generator.
findings.recommended_fix: After each content_bbox call assert positive dims and in-canvas bounds; abort loudly on violation.

findings.title: add_outline docstring claims plate top 'flush at the fill's base' — flat fills hover 0.01 above it (only gable eaves are flush)
findings.detail: Plate top z=0.02; flat quads/discs sit at FILL_Z=0.03 (the hover avoids coplanar z-fighting); gable base_z=OUTLINE_H is the only flush case. Docstring overclaims. Sub-pixel at render scale — doc accuracy only.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: plate sits 0.01 below the flat fill plane; gable eaves rest flush.

findings.title: KYLE §3 hue targets ship only as optional-swap comments; the ≥15° blur-test hue-separation cure is not tracked as an explicit merge-gate item
findings.detail: Documented, deliberate deferral (PR body: palette migration is the in-engine wave's surface; SPEC comments say 'confirm against the node-clarity palette at merge') — but the blur-test cure itself has no tracked gate anywhere. Worth an explicit line so the merge-LAST resolution actually checks it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the ≥15° hue-separation check as an explicit fold-in/merge checklist item in the spec.

findings.title: Per-sprite camera pads live outside the SPEC table; an oversized SPEC footprint silently clips at the 256px frame edge — still present since round 1
